rules.quote: Only add colons that are essential.
rules.specification: The page does not define an objective test for ‘essential’. Do not equate a grammatically optional colon with an unnecessary one, or generate a second finding for an error covered by a more specific colon rule.
rules.violation_condition: A colon is unnecessary in its context.
rules.why: G-4: the heading and body repeat the same restraint; the undefined necessity criterion remains explicit.

covers.quote: Use a colon to:
introduce a word, phrase or clause that provides more detail
introduce a question
give an example
summarise or contrast with what comes before it.
A sentence fragment can come before the colon if the fragment can stand alone or if it’s introducing a bulleted list.

parts.quote: Use correct spelling: check a dictionary if you need to.
Our work is about answering this simple question: how?
We’ll have to use a stronger tool: sanctions.
This is the guiding principle for our workplace: collaboration.
The committee found there was only one possible explanation: fraud.
Warning: strong winds forecast for Sydney today.

rules.quote: Introduce examples and contrasts with colons
rules.specification: Interpret this as punctuation between a lead-in and the material it introduces, not a requirement to insert a colon into every sentence that provides detail or makes a contrast.
rules.violation_condition: A lead-in lacks a colon separating it from following material presented as an elaboration, question, example, summary or contrast.
when: The following material gives more detail, introduces a question, gives an example, or summarises or contrasts with the preceding text.
A sentence fragment may precede the colon if it can stand alone or introduces a bulleted list.
List lead-ins, subtitles, block quotations and mathematical ratios have separate, more specific checks.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the listed relationships are cases of the same introduction check; G-3 keeps the fragment permission as a condition.

covers.quote: Use a colon to introduce a list of words, phrases or clauses.
Include the colon to restructure content into bulleted lists.

parts.quote: Pick any 2 of the 3: low price, high speed, high quality.
The position has these requirements: strong communication skills and experience across content management platforms.
We need to:
check Appendix A of the report
ask Mary about the final chapter of her book
rewrite our introduction.
The requirements for the position are:
strong communication skills
experience across content management platforms.

rules.violation_condition: A lead-in introducing a list lacks a colon, other than an inline list that flows on as part of the sentence.
when: The list contains words, phrases or clauses.
Do not require a colon for an inline list that flows on as part of a full sentence.
A colon is required when content is restructured as a bulleted list, even if the original inline version did not take one.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: list types and restructuring into bullets change the conditions of one missing-colon check.

parts.quote: Pick any 2 of low price, high speed and high quality.
The requirements for the position are strong communication skills and experience across content management platforms.
Pick any 2 of: low price, high speed and high quality.
The requirements for the position are: strong communication skills and experience across content management platforms.

rules.quote: Don’t include a colon when the list flows on as part of a full sentence.
rules.violation_condition: A colon interrupts an inline list that flows on syntactically as part of the surrounding sentence.
when: The list is inline and forms part of a full sentence.
This prohibition does not apply after restructuring the content as a bulleted list.
rules.why: This flags an intrusive colon, not the missing lead-in colon flagged by the preceding rule; E-2 attaches the Correct/Incorrect pairs here.

covers.quote: Use lower case following a colon in most cases
the word that follows the colon is a proper noun
the text after the colon is a question that is a complete sentence.
After a colon, capitalise the first word of questions that are complete sentences.
Follow the colon with a lower case letter, unless it’s a proper noun.

parts.quote: We had to write 66 reports: it took months.
The commander was confident: Special Air Service Regiment had enough ammunition.
We had to write many reports: It took months.
The commander was confident: special air service regiment had enough ammunition.
The election was fought on a simple question: Which party had the best economic credentials?
The election was fought on a simple question: which party had the best economic credentials?
Teaching in Australia: a deep dive into the education system
Stanovich KE (1986) ‘Matthew effects in reading: some consequences of individual differences in the acquisition of literacy’, Reading Research Quarterly, 21(4):360–407.

rules.quote: Start the word after the colon with a lower case letter unless:
rules.violation_condition: The first word continuing after a colon has the wrong initial case: an unnecessary capital in ordinary text, a lowercase proper noun, or a lowercase initial in a question that is a complete sentence.
when: Use lower case by default for text continuing after a colon.
A proper noun retains its capitalisation.
A question that is a complete sentence starts with a capital letter.
The lower-case convention also applies after the colon introducing a book or article subtitle, unless the following word is a proper noun.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: default case, proper nouns, complete questions and the subtitle restatement belong to one post-colon case check.

parts.quote: They answered the question:
They wrote 23 reports.
Each report took 11 days to write.

rules.quote: If the colon introduces a series of sentences or questions, use a lead-in and colon to introduce them in a bulleted or numbered list.
rules.violation_condition: A colon introduces a series of sentences or questions in running text rather than as a bulleted or numbered list.
when: The colon introduces more than one sentence or question.
The series should be presented as list items following a lead-in ending in a colon.
A missing colon on an existing list lead-in is handled by the list-introduction rule.
rules.why: This is a distinct list-structure check, not another capitalisation rule or a duplicate missing-colon check; E-3 keeps the lead-in and items together.

rules.quote: Start subtitles of books and articles with a colon
rules.violation_condition: A book or article title has a subtitle that is not separated from the main title by a colon.
when: A book or article has a subtitle.
This applies both when writing about the work and when referencing it.
Capitalisation after the subtitle colon is handled by the post-colon case rule.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: prose mentions and references are conditions of the same subtitle-separator check.

rules.violation_condition: A block quotation's lead-in does not end with a colon.
when: A lead-in introduces a block quotation.
